title: Indirect LED Ceiling Lighting for an Exposed-Ceiling Timber-Frame Space (This Old House)
summary: This Old House explores preserving an original timber-frame great room while upgrading the ceiling and lighting. The episode discusses the challenges of lighting a kitchen-dining-great-room combination with a historically restored ceiling and a pitched roof, balancing task and general lighting with the desire to reveal rather than conceal original materials. The plan centers on hidden LED tape running along the beams to create a bright, indirect glow, while pendant lighting and careful mounting strategies are evaluated to avoid visual clutter and respect the historic structure.

sections.title: Project Vision: Preserve historic material while planning lighting
concepts: retaining old beams, wall plates, rafters, and sheathing
illusion of original building in a modern framed space
lighting considerations tied to historical integrity
sections.description: The hosts emphasize preserving the original timber-frame and roof materials to maintain historical integrity, noting that old ceiling boards will be reinstalled beneath new framing to preserve the space’s look. The discussion highlights anticipated challenges across insulation, lighting, and integration with modern systems.

sections.title: Lighting strategy for a pitched ceiling and pendant options
concepts: options for hanging pendants: ceiling vs. beam
mounting from original floor joists to define kitchen area
sections.description: A mock-up demonstrates a 45° roof pitch with a 12/pitch ratio, illustrating the limitations of typical recessed fixtures and the exploration of pendant lighting either from the ceiling or low from a beam. The team proposes hanging from the original floor joists to both provide support and delineate the kitchen area while keeping the ceiling visually uncluttered.

sections.title: Indirect LED lighting plan and live demonstration
concepts: LED tape installation on top of beams
indirect lighting to illuminate the ceiling glow
sections.description: The crew introduces LED tape as a hidden lighting solution that will run along the tops of the beams to create a bright glow without exposing fixtures. A demonstration of a single LED strip confirms it produces surprising brightness, with the plan calling for eight times that amount across the ceiling to achieve a warm, indirect illumination that enhances the timber surfaces.
